name: hereditary cancer overview
title: Hereditary cancer: red flags on a three-generation family history prompt referral for genetic counselling when a test could change management and the patient wants it; test an affected relative first, then unaffected adult relatives, never children for adult-onset conditions; a BRCA1/2 result leads to surveillance or prophylactic surgery for women and men

root.title: Cancer in the patient or family: could it be HEREDITARY, and WHO do I test?
lines: most cancer is SPORADIC (one somatic cell, NOT passed on) or FAMILIAL (shared genes + environment)
take ≥ 3 generations on BOTH sides: cancer types, age at diagnosis, new primary or metastasis

groups.title: A RED FLAG → suspect HEREDITARY (a mutation in EVERY cell, inherited)
lines: early onset (breast < 50, ovarian < 60) · several primaries in one person · several relatives on ONE side · a family pattern · Ashkenazi Jewish ancestry (BRCA1/2)

pres.title: REFER for genetic counselling if ALL of these
lines: • personal or family history of cancer
• a test exists and its result can be interpreted
• the result could change management, AND the patient wants to know

test: 2 · Offer testing only AFTER the mutation is confirmed

rows: BRCA1/2 POSITIVE: hereditary breast and ovarian cancer (HBOC)
